rationale: B wins because its proof gates are actual stop signs, not stage dressing: "Do not pitch this without the harness" would keep a founder from walking into a benchmark correction. A has plenty of structure, but "Offline AI That Runs on a Laptop Is Now Good Enough for a Fortune 100 Factory" promotes a manufacturer citation into a factory/offline deployment claim the facts do not support. B still has two bad leaps, especially "behind its own firewall," but it gives the founder more usable beat targets and the right first next step.
gaps_in_A: "Offline AI That Runs on a Laptop Is Now Good Enough for a Fortune 100 Factory" overclaims the supplied facts: the update gives a Fortune 100 manufacturer customer, not a factory use case or proof the offline model is running there.
"The Factory That Runs AI Without a Cloud Connection" repeats the same unsupported plant-floor/offline story. Two wrappers on the same invented customer narrative is padding with a hard hat.

"Enterprises Can Deploy This AI Without Owing Anyone a Subscription" is too broad. Apache 2.0 supports a licensing angle, but the update also launches a paid enterprise tier, so the claim needs to be narrowed to the model itself.
The next step jumps to "journalist-fit-check" when the benchmark and customer-use claims still need fact-checking and customer confirmation first.
gaps_in_B: "A Fortune 100 manufacturer is running Hugging Face models behind its own firewall" is not in the update. Private model hosting plus a manufacturer customer does not equal behind-the-firewall deployment.
"Two million models, and no easy way to know which ones are safe to use" invents a safety/provenance problem without evidence. B admits it is thin, but the headline still outruns the facts.

"Hugging Face bets the next AI workload never leaves the device" overstates a single on-device release into a broad workload thesis. It needs measured device performance before it can carry that altitude.
"whether Apache 2.0 covers the weights, the training code, or both" is a fair diligence question only if the release materials are ambiguous. The supplied fact simply says the model is Apache 2.0.
